sections.title: 二、綜合測驗（占10分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第11題至第20題，每題1分。

groups.passage:
Glaciers are usually associated with colder climates. But some mountain ranges of South America, Africa, and Indonesia are also [[11]] glaciers and ice sheets. These tropical glaciers serve as a major source of water supply to one-sixth of the world’s population.
A newly published study, however, revealed that rising temperatures are posing an [[12]] threat to the last tropical glaciers in Indonesia’s Papua region. The ice sheets, which once spanned 20 square kilometers, are thinning over five times as quickly compared to a few years ago. [[13]] already shrunk by 85% to a mere 0.5 square kilometers, Papua’s glaciers will completely disappear within a decade, researchers have predicted.
The disappearance of the glaciers will also leave a significant [[14]] impact. For many indigenous Papuans, the ice sheets represent a sacred symbol. “The mountains and valleys are the arms and legs of their god and the glaciers are the head,” explained the head researcher.
The study warned that Papua’s glaciers are only the “first to go” if greenhouse gases are [[15]] and temperatures continue rising. And this is certainly a serious warning about the depressing fate of other glaciers around the world.

tags.topic: disappearing tropical glaciers in Papua, Indonesia

groups.passage:
Airline passengers may have noticed that all plane windows have rounded edges, instead of the hard corners commonly found in our house. The round windows are indeed pleasant to the eye, but they actually were designed for reasons [[16]] aesthetics.
In the early days of aviation, plane windows [[17]] square in shape. Then as commercial air travel became popular in the 1950s and airplanes began flying higher and faster, three planes mysteriously broke apart in midair. The cause? Square windows. Scientists found that sharp corners are natural weak spots where stress concentrates. The problem is [[18]] when airplanes fly at higher altitudes, where the difference between the inside and outside pressure increases, causing added stress. When subjected to repeated pressurization high in the sky, the four corners on a square window may [[19]].
Curved windows, on the other hand, distribute stress around more evenly, reducing the likelihood of cracks or breaks. Circular shapes are also stronger and resist deformation, and therefore can [[20]] extreme differences in pressure inside and outside of an aircraft.
Thus, round windows are a major safety innovation that keeps planes from disintegrating mid-flight. They are also used on ships and spacecraft for their greater structural integrity.

sections.title: 三、文意選填（占10分）
sections.instructions: 說明：第21題至第30題為單選題，每題1分。

groups.passage:
A stunt person is a man or a woman who performs dangerous acts, usually in the television or movie industry. In this line of work, the person is paid to do daring actions that are deemed too [[21]] for the regular actor to perform, including jumping from heights, crashing cars, or fighting with weapons.
Stunt work emerged out of [[22]] over time. In the early days of the film industry, actors themselves shot acrobatic acts and dangerous scenes, until they began to get injured. There were, however, no [[23]] crew members to perform impressive stunts at that time. If something dangerous needed to be done for a scene, the producers would hire anyone crazy or desperate enough to do it. These people were not trained to perform stunts, so they often [[24]] things for the first time during the actual shooting. They had to learn from their own mistakes, which [[25]] some their lives, and almost all suffered light or severe injuries.
Beginning around 1910, audiences developed a taste for serial action movies, which [[26]] the use of dedicated stunt people to perform in dangerous scenes. Such demand increased with the rise of western movies, and many cowboys with masterful skills on horseback found a new [[27]] as a stunt person. Tom Mix and Yakima Canutt were among the most famous. The 1960s and ’70s [[28]] the development of most modern stunt technology, like air rams and bullet squibs. That technology has continued to evolve into the present.
Today, CGI (computer generated imagery) is widely used in filmmaking, and it is now [[29]] to create very lifelike scenes without using real stunt people. However, CGI has difficulties of its own, and there will always be a demand for the realism and thrilling [[30]] of an actual stunt. So the stunt industry is probably in no immediate danger of dying off.

sections.title: 四、篇章結構（占8分）
sections.instructions: 說明：說明︰第31題至第34題為單選題，每題2分。

groups.passage:
Roller coasters have been known for their agonizingly slow starts, near heart-stopping drops and scream-inducing turns and loops. [[31]]
The designers must first consider what kind of riders will use the coaster. If the coaster is designed for small children, the hills and curves will be gentle, and the car speed will be relatively slow. Families usually want a somewhat faster ride with plenty of turns and moderate force. Ultimate thrill seekers want extreme heights and speed.
[[32]] Roller coasters usually take up a lot of room not only on the ground but also in the air. Designers must take into consideration surrounding rides, power lines, and other obstacles. Some amusement parks have added so many rides that a new roller coaster has to be designed to make its way through existing rides and walkways.
The next objective for the designers is to achieve a unique “feel” for the coaster. [[33]] Once up the incline, the first drop is usually designed to be the steepest, and therefore the fastest and scariest. Other drops can be designed with a brief flattened section in the middle, and are called double dips. Drops with very abrupt transitions to a flat or upturned section are called slammers because they slam the passengers down into their seats. Letting the cars run close to the ground, in what is called a gully coaster, gives the illusion of increased speed.
[[34]] Only after its safety is assured can the design be used to build a new roller coaster.

options_bank.A: Designers must then consider the space available for the coaster.
options_bank.B: Building an exciting roller coaster starts with a brilliant design.
options_bank.C: Theme and type are also important aspects to consider in coaster design.
options_bank.D: Designers can draw on a number of techniques to provide a memorable ride.
options_bank.E: When the design is complete, detailed calculation and careful testing procedures will follow.

sections.title: 五、閱讀測驗（占24分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第35題至第46題，每題2分。

groups.passage:
The flip-flop is the simplest shoe on the planet. It consists of a piece of rubber, plastic, leather, or woven material in the outline of a foot, with a strap holding the sandal to a wearer’s toes. The name comes from the sound the sandals make when they slap the walking feet.
The earliest record of people wearing the flip-flop comes from Egypt, but many ancient cultures had their own variants of the footwear. In the Greek version, the toe strap ran between the first and second toes, while Roman sandals had the strap between the second and third toes. The Mesopotamians wore the strap between the third and fourth toes. In India, “toe knob” sandals had a knob between the first and second toes.
Modern flip-flops derive from Japanese zōris, which were often worn with socks dividing the big toe from the rest, and were typically made of rice straw. During World War II, Japan seized much of Southeast Asia’s rubber. In 1945, devastated from the war, the country set about establishing a cheap industry that could rebuild its economy. The Japanese used their rubber reserves from the war to mass-produce the simplest Japanese footwear. Rubber thus replaced rice straw as the major material for the flip-flop.
In the 1950s, flip-flops became popular in the United States as soldiers returning from occupied Japan brought zōris home. The sandals have subsequently undergone redesign, often appearing in bright colors in line with Californian beach culture. They have remained popular due to their convenience, and are often worn with bathing suits or summer clothing. Some people also wear dressy versions for more formal occasions.
Despite their popularity, flip-flops provoke some questions. Their simple design is responsible for many foot injuries. Another issue is the suitability of exposing feet on the street and places other than the beach. But even more serious is their environmental impact: Millions of plastic discards end up in landfills or the ocean, releasing chemicals and at the same time taking centuries to decompose.

groups.passage:
Ships are the lifeline of trade among countries. Almost everything, from food to machinery, comes by way of the sea in huge ships piloted by captains. But the captain of a ship is responsible for guiding the vessel until they hit a port, waiting to enter the harbor. The task of bringing the ship into the harbor and anchoring it is taken up by a different captain. This captain is called a marine pilot.
A marine pilot is a boat pilot with specialized knowledge of a particular port or harbor. The pilot is needed to direct large ships into a port, where there are often deep water channels surrounded by shallower seabeds. Without the services of a marine pilot, docking ships would be hazardous. There would be a real chance of running aground and damaging the ship and the cargo, some of which might be dangerous if released into a water-based ecosystem.
In addition to the shallower seabeds, tide and wind pose further challenges for bringing ships into a port. During different tides, currents may change from one direction to the other. The same strategy for docking a vessel during an incoming tide may not work during an outgoing tide. Also, the wind can significantly alter the direction of the ship and how it reacts, adding to the difficulty of anchoring the ship.
Marine pilotage is a job that requires a high degree of proficiency as well as quick and independent thinking. Above all, it is about risk management. A marine pilot goes on board at a crucial time and controls the vessel based on his or her knowledge of the port and the situation at hand. The pilot is responsible for not only the safety of the ship but also the protection of the port and the marine environment.

groups.passage:
Zebrafish, named for their characteristic stripes, have been a popular test subject for researchers. Only a few centimeters in length, the fish breed easily in captivity, grow quickly, and their transparent body makes it easy to study their organs. Above all, they possess some amazing “self-healing” power. When part of their heart is removed, they can grow it back in a matter of weeks. When blinded, they can quickly regain the ability to see.
Recent studies show that humans and zebrafish have the same major organs and share 70 percent of the genes. Moreover, 84 percent of human genes associated with disease find a counterpart in zebrafish. Scientists thus hope that understanding the self-healing mystery of the fish may one day allow humans to regenerate such organs as eyes, hearts, and spines.
Researchers at Vanderbilt University are particularly interested in zebrafish retina regeneration. They have learned that damage of retina can cause blindness in zebrafish, yet it only takes about three to four weeks before vision is restored. The structure and cell types of zebrafish retinas are almost identical to those of humans. If the process can be replicated in humans, it may give rise to new treatments for blindness caused by retinal damage.
In order to know exactly how zebrafish retina is regenerated, the team looked at the neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), a chemical messenger in the brain that reduces the activity of neurons. They found that lowering GABA levels in zebrafish can trigger retina regeneration, while a high level of GABA concentration will suppress the regeneration process. This suggested that GABA plays an important role in the fish’s ability to regain their sight.
The team is beginning to test the GABA theory on mice. If that works, human trials will be next on the agenda. If the research proves successful in humans, some of the nearly 40 million blind people worldwide may one day have a tiny, striped fish to thank.

groups.passage: To support refugees and people facing crises around the world, the International Olympic Committee created the Refugee Olympic Team. Refugee athletes have been invited to compete in the Olympic Games since 2016. Here are two refugee athletes and their stories.

passage_parts.label: left
passage_parts.text:
Yusra Mardini is a swimmer who grew up in the war-torn country of Syria. Due to the unstable political situation there, Yusra sometimes had to train in pools under roofs that had been blown open by bombings.
In 2015 when she was just a 17-year-old, her house was destroyed in the civil war, so she decided to flee her home country. She managed to reach Turkey through Lebanon. From Turkey, she boarded a small boat that held 20 people and set sail into the deep waters of the Aegean Sea. But 30 minutes later, the engine stopped and the boat began to sink. Yusra dove into the cold water, and—with the help of her sister and two men—swam and pushed the boat for over three hours to reach the Greek island of Lesbos. They saved everyone aboard.
Yusra eventually settled in Germany and has since worked to inspire others to pursue their dreams. Her incredible story and superior swimming skills won her the opportunity to participate in the Olympic Games. She was a member of the Refugee Olympic Team for both the 2016 Rio Games and 2021 Tokyo Games.

passage_parts.label: right
passage_parts.text:
Popole Misenga was born in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. When he was nine, the country’s civil war claimed the life of his mother and left him homeless. Escaping from the war zone, he wandered alone for a week in a rainforest before being rescued and taken to a center for displaced children in the capital, Kinshasa.
There, Popole discovered judo, from which he gained strength in body and mind. “Judo helped me by giving me serenity, discipline, commitment—everything,” he said. He trained hard and became a professional judoka. However, each time he lost a competition, his coaches would lock him in a cage for days, feeding him only coffee and bread. Finally, when he was cruelly abused for not winning medals at the 2013 World Championships in Brazil, he decided to seek protection.
Popole was granted asylum in 2014 by Brazilian government and later continued judo training at a youth facility. He made his Olympic debut at Rio 2016. He also represented the Refugee Olympic Team in 2021 Tokyo Games.

figures.description: 黑白照片：一座兒童遊樂場式的公園。地面鋪設方格狀的軟質安全地墊，畫面左側是由金屬柱與橫桿組成的攀爬遊具（有吊掛的攀爬網、垂吊繩與一排可踩踏的蘑菇形踏墊），中後方是大型組合式溜滑梯遊具（有圓頂塔樓、拱門、攀爬網與數條溜滑梯，最右側是兩道並排的溜滑梯），右側邊緣有一張小椅子、長椅與幾個圓形踏墩；周圍只有少數灌木，天空晴朗有少許雲朵，畫面中沒有人。

figures.description: 黑白照片：一座綠意盎然的自然型公園。前景是一大片灑落樹蔭的草地，數棵高大的樹木錯落其間（左前方一棵樹幹上掛著小牌子），中景有一圈低矮的灌木與花叢，遠處是陽光照亮的開闊草坪（有一塊明亮的空地）與更多樹林，天空明亮，畫面中沒有人，也沒有人工遊樂設施。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem: 提示︰不同的公園，可能樣貌不同，特色也不同。請以此為主題，並依據下列兩張圖片的內容，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段描述圖 A 和圖 B 中的公園各有何特色，第二段則說明你心目中理想公園的樣貌與特色，並解釋你的理由。
questions.scoring_notes:
評分原則：
1.多寫段，不扣分。
2.字數嚴重不足，扣1分。
英文作文評分指標（等級：優／可／差／劣）
內容：優（5-4分）＝主題（句）清楚切題，並有具體、完整的相關細節支持。／可（3分）＝主題不夠清楚或突顯，部分相關敘述發展不全。／差（2-1分）＝主題不明，大部分相關敘述發展不全或與主題無關。／劣（0分）＝文不對題或沒寫（凡文不對題或沒寫者，其他各項均以零分計算）。
組織：優（5-4分）＝重點分明，有開頭、發展、結尾，前後連貫，轉承語使用得當。／可（3分）＝重點安排不妥，前後發展比例與轉承語使用欠妥。／差（2-1分）＝重點不明、前後不連貫。／劣（0分）＝全文毫無組織或未按提示寫作。
文法、句構：優（5-4分）＝全文幾無文法、格式、標點錯誤，文句結構富變化。／可（3分）＝文法、格式、標點錯誤少，且未影響文意之表達。／差（2-1分）＝文法、格式、標點錯誤多，且明顯影響文意之表達。／劣（0分）＝全文文法錯誤嚴重，導致文意不明。
字彙、拼字：優（5-4分）＝用字精確、得宜，且幾無拼字、大小寫錯誤。／可（3分）＝字詞單調、重複，用字偶有不當，少許拼字、大小寫錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。／差（2-1分）＝用字、拼字、大小寫錯誤多，明顯影響文意之表達。／劣（0分）＝只寫出或抄襲與題意有關的零碎字詞。
（試題解析 other-4.pdf 的評分原則：英文作文依考生在內容、組織、文法句構、字彙拼字之表現評分，各項得分加總後給予一個整體分數（holistic score），再依總分1至20分，分為下述五等級：特優（19-20分）、優（15-18分）、可（10-14分）、差（5-9分）、劣（0-4分）。閱卷委員在仔細評閱考生的作答內容後，再依其內容是否切題、組織是否具連貫性、句子結構與文法、用字是否適切表達文意，及拼字是否正確等要項，進行評分；為確保評分一致性，在試閱時，閱卷委員皆必須完全熟悉及理解各分項的評分標準（分項說明詳見表一）。字數明顯不足者，扣總分1分；未分段者，亦扣總分1分。試題解析：評量考生能否運用所學詞彙、句法，寫出一篇文長至少120個單詞，且具一致性和連貫性的英文作文。寫作之主題生活化，內容與公園的樣貌與特色有關，考生根據所提供的圖片內容及作答提示，寫一篇英文作文。文分兩段，第一段描述圖片場景中所呈現的公園景物與特色；第二段則說明心目中理想的公園的樣貌與特色，並解釋自己的理由。）

extraction.method: pdftotext -layout 與 pdftotext（無 -layout）擷取題本 paper.pdf、參考答案及評分原則 scoring.pdf、答題卷 other-1.pdf、參考試卷說明 other-3.pdf、試題解析 other-4.pdf；混合題左右兩欄以 pdftotext -x/-y/-W/-H 分欄裁切擷取；選文段落依 -layout 縮排切分，空格以程式替換為 [[題號]] 並核對個數；Read 看題本第3–14頁與 scoring.pdf 全部4頁的頁面影像，逐一確認段落、說明文字、第35題涼鞋插圖、混合題雙欄版面與標誌、作文圖A／圖B、中譯英大括號替換寫法與作文評分指標表；另以程式將重複使用的歷屆考題與 gsat-109/110/112 已解析 JSON 及 gsat-105/111 題本文字逐字比對；查證者（verifier）另以 pdftotext -layout／raw 與 -x/-y/-W/-H 分欄裁切重新擷取，逐題比對134個選項、全部題幹與8篇選文（含混合題左右兩欄逐詞比對、段落數與 [[題號]] 位置），Read 看題本第4–14頁與 scoring.pdf 第1–4頁影像逐題核對答案，pdfimages 取出第35題插圖與作文圖A／圖B放大核對描述
issues: 結構核對（gsat-spec.json current，115學年度起適用考試說明）：第壹部分選擇題62分一致——詞彙1–10、綜合測驗11–20（2題組×5空）、文意選填21–30每題1分；篇章結構31–34每題2分且選項(A)–(E)共5個（含1個干擾句），符合115起「4空格搭配5選項」新制；閱讀35–46每題2分（3題組×4題）。第參部分非選擇題28分一致（中譯英2題各4分、英文作文20分、至少120個單詞、文分兩段）。總分100、考試時間100分鐘（封面作答注意事項）。

結構差異（以題本為準）：第貳部分混合題同為1題組10分，但題號是47–49而非 spec current typical_layout_112_115 的47–50——第47題為兩格填空 (A)、(B)（「填空，4分」，評分原則每格2／1／0分）、第48題簡答2分、第49題多選題4分（選項(A)–(F)）。此版型與111學年度學測（spec mixed.by_year.111）相同；本題組即沿用111學年度學測第47–49題。
第47題兩格依 schema 拆為 no=47、label「47A」「47B」兩個小題，各2分（評分原則與答案檔標為47(A)、47(B)）；validator 的「題號重複 [1, 2, 47]」warning 中的47由此而來。題本空格印成底線的「(A)」「(B)」，stem 中寫成 [[47A]]、[[47B]]；兩小題 stem 都放入完整作答說明與兩個句子。

混合題參考答案：評分原則每題列兩行。47(A) 列 participating、swimming，answer 取第一行 participating，swimming 放 accepted_answers；47(B) 列 abuse、cruelty/cruelties，answer＝abuse，accepted_answers＝[cruelty, cruelties]；48 列 asylum、Asylum.（大寫加句點的完整作答形式），answer＝asylum，accepted_answers 逐字保留「Asylum.」。scoring_notes 收錄混合題評分原則表（2分／1分／0分）與該題參考答案原排版。第49題官方答案 CD（多選題計分依封面「多選題計分方式」），答題卷 other-1.pdf 第49題劃記區為 A–F。

混合題選文版面：引言段（含右上角 Refugee Olympic Team 標誌）後，兩位選手的故事以無標題的左右兩欄表格並列。引言放 passage；兩則故事放 passage_parts，label 用「left」「right」（解析稱左欄／右欄），title 為 null（題本沒有標題，未自行加上）；兩欄文字以 pdftotext 分欄裁切取得，並與頁面影像核對段落。標誌只作裝飾，以文字描述放在 figures。
統計：參考試卷不是正式施測的考卷，大考中心沒有發布統計檔（units.json 也沒有 stats），所有小題 stats 為 null、sources.stats 為空陣列；validator 的「整份考卷沒有任何統計資料」warning 由此而來，屬預期。下述重複使用的試題在原考試年度有統計，但那不是本試卷的數據，未搬過來。

答案來源：本試卷沒有獨立的答案檔，選擇題答案取自「參考答案及評分原則」scoring.pdf 第壹部分的參考答案表（看頁面影像核對），因此 sources.answer 與 sources.scoring 都指向 scoring.pdf。46題選擇題與第49題答案都與試題解析 other-4.pdf 一致，也與各題原出處考試的官方答案一致（111：1,4,7,8,9,10,16–30,43–46,49；105：10；109：3,41–48；110：14,26–30；112：1）。

重複使用的歷屆試題（參考試卷說明 other-3.pdf：「本次試題除部分為原創外，亦有採用或修改歷年考題或研究用試題情形」）：以擴充欄位 reused_from 標在小題上。對應：1←111-1、2←105-10、3←112-1、4←109-3、5←111-4、6←111-8、7←110-14、8←111-7、9←111-10、10←111-9；11–15←110-26–30（冰河題組）；16–20←111-16–20（飛機窗戶）；21–30←111-21–30（特技替身）；35–38←109-41–44（夾腳拖）；39–42←109-45–48（引水人）；43–46←111-43–46（斑馬魚）；47–49←111-47–49（難民奧運代表隊）；中譯英1–2←110 中譯英1–2；英文作文←111 英文作文（公園）。以程式逐詞比對（gsat-109/110/112 已解析 JSON、gsat-111 Word 版 paper-2.docx、gsat-105 題本文字）：題幹、選項、選文與選項順序都完全相同，只有詞彙題的題序重排。只有篇章結構31–34（雲霄飛車設計）在 repo 內學測83–115、指考91–110題本中找不到，試題解析列網路資料出處、未註明自創，可能是研究用試題或新命題。跨年分析時應避免重複計算這些題目。

重複題的標註沿用已解析考卷，保持一致：11–15沿用 gsat-110 第26–30題（含14題 test_point=discourse）；35–42沿用 gsat-109 第41–48題的 item_type——第35題用 application（看插圖判斷涼鞋屬於哪個文化，本卷解析說是「找尋特定的資訊」），第40題用 inference（選文講潮汐與風，選項寫 weather conditions，本卷解析說是「內容細節」）；兩組題組的 sdgs 也沿用（夾腳拖 [12,14]、引水人 [14]）。中譯英 patterns／topic 沿用 gsat-110。

中譯英參考答案：評分原則用大括號並列可替換的寫法。第1題 {over | more than}、{around the world | globally}、{lost their lives | died | were killed}，answer 取各括號第一個寫法，其餘11種組合放 accepted_answers；第2題 {Therefore, | Because of this,}、{laws | regulations}，以及可省略的「(all)」，answer 取第一個寫法並保留 all，其餘7種組合（含省略 all 的寫法）放 accepted_answers。scoring_notes 以 {A | B} 記號逐字保留原排版，並附試題解析 other-4.pdf 對該題的說明。
中譯英評分原則第3條兩份官方文件寫法不同：scoring.pdf 寫「相同之拼字錯誤，只扣一次。」，試題解析 other-4.pdf 寫「相同之拼字錯誤或文法錯誤，只扣一次。」。scoring_notes 照 scoring.pdf。中文與數字之間的排版空格（如「總分 8 分」）未保留。

英文作文：scoring.pdf 的評分原則只有「1.多寫段，不扣分。2.字數嚴重不足，扣 1 分。」和「英文作文評分指標」表，表格依「項目：等級（分數）＝描述」轉成文字。試題解析 other-4.pdf 另有整體評分說明（holistic score、五個等級，以及「字數明顯不足者，扣總分1分；未分段者，亦扣總分1分」），與 scoring.pdf 的「多寫段，不扣分」並不衝突，一併附在 scoring_notes 並註明出處。官方沒有範文，answer 為 null。
題號：中譯英在題本印為 1.、2.，作文沒有題號；schema 要求 no 為整數，所以中譯英 no＝1、2，作文 no＝1，label 改為「中譯英1」「中譯英2」「英文作文」，以免和詞彙題1、2重複（與 gsat-115 相同做法）。

說明文字逐字保留：篇章結構的說明在題本中就重複了一次「說明」，寫作「說明：說明︰第31題至第34題為單選題，每題2分。」（看頁面影像確認），照原樣保留。冒號也照文字層原樣：詞彙、綜合、閱讀、混合題、作文與「提示︰」用「︰」(U+FE30)，文意選填、篇章結構開頭、第參部分與中譯英用「：」(U+FF1A)。詞彙、綜合、閱讀的說明沒有「為單選題」字樣，文意選填與篇章結構有，照題本保留。混合題說明為「並依規定用筆作答」（115正式試卷為「並以規定用筆作答」）。

空白與底線：大題標題的字距空格（如「第 壹 部 分」「一 、 詞 彙 題 （ 占 10分 ）」）已去除；說明、題幹中的中英、中數之間空格照文字層和頁面影像保留（「本部分共有 1 題組」「圖 A 和圖 B」「對Yusra Mardini 和 Popole Misenga都」）。第2題題本為「before ______ , since」，空格線與逗號之間的空白照印刷保留；各題空格線長短不一，一律寫成「______」；第6題空格前多出的排版空白已合併。
格式：粗體（a crucial time〔選文與第41題〕、replicated〔選文與第45題〕、第38、46題的 NOT、第47題「一個單詞（word）」粗體加底線）與斜體（zōris）都不保留格式；沒有題目問畫底線的字，所以沒有 <u> 標記。混合題右欄引文「commitment—everything」的破折號在 PDF 中位於行尾，接回時沒有加空白。
圖片：第35題涼鞋插圖、作文圖A（遊樂設施公園）與圖B（樹林草地公園）、混合題標誌都已看頁面影像，用文字描述放在題組 figures。第35題插圖描述寫出趾帶位於第二、三趾之間，這是作答所需資訊；依選文可對應 Roman，與官方答案D一致。

標註補充：第46題要判斷事實或意見，item_type 沒有對應值，暫用 inference；第17題 used to be 標 grammar／modal；47A／47B 為摘要句填空，item_type 與 gsat-112–115 混合題填空一致，用 synthesis；48為 vocab_in_context，49為 synthesis（依解析「整合文章內容，將不同的訊息分類、歸納與比較」）。sdgs：冰河 [6,13]（沿用 gsat-110）、斑馬魚與失明治療 [3]、難民選手 [10,16]、中譯英道路安全 [3,11]、作文公園綠地 [11]；飛機窗戶、特技替身、雲霄飛車為 []。
來源檔：other-1.pdf（答題卷）、other-3.pdf（參考試卷說明）、other-4.pdf（試題解析）有用到，列在 sources.other；other-2.pdf（A4 版答題卷）與 other-5／other-6（考試說明）沒有用到，未列入。

查證（verifier）：選擇題46題與第49題答案逐題對照 scoring.pdf 第1頁答案表影像，全部正確；47(A)、47(B)、48 參考答案與 scoring.pdf 第2頁一致；中譯英參考答案與第3頁大括號排版一致。134個選項、全部題幹、8篇選文（含混合題左右兩欄）與 pdftotext 逐詞比對無差異，段落數與空格位置正確。本卷沒有統計檔，無法抽查統計。修正：第35題插圖描述原寫「由腳踝以下」，但插圖畫到小腿下半段且有一圈踝帶，已改寫；作文圖B描述原寫「遠處有一小片水面」，放大原圖看不出是水面（較像陽光照亮的空地或步道），改為不臆測的寫法。
試題解析 other-4.pdf 把詞彙題1–10、中譯英與英文作文的「資料出處」都標為「自創」，但這些題目與上述歷屆學測試題逐字相同；「自創」應是指大考中心自行命題（不是改寫自外部資料），不影響 reused_from 的對應。綜合測驗、文意選填、篇章結構、閱讀與混合題則列網路資料出處。
